bib.title: Graph-R1: Towards Agentic GraphRAG Framework via End-to-end Reinforcement Learning

legacy_report:
SOURCE: "Graph-R1: Towards Agentic GraphRAG Framework via End-to-end Reinforcement Learning", Haoran Luo, Haihong E, Guanting Chen, Qika Lin, Yikai Guo, Fangzhi Xu, Zemin Kuang, Meina Song, Xiaobao Wu, Yifan Zhu, Luu Anh Tuan. arXiv 2507.21892v2 (2 Jun 2026); the footer says PMLR 306, 2026 (ICML, Seoul). Title verified on p.1. Code: github.com/LHRLAB/Graph-R1.

COVERAGE: All 21 pages read (about 100,247 chars). Main text, appendices A to K, and the case study were read. The reference list was skimmed. The Figure 8/10 prompt text and the Table 4 case-study text were only partly read. Appendices I and J (cut off in the extraction) were not read in full. Only the tail of J, a construction-pipeline description (appendix letter unconfirmed), was read.

CLAIMS (ranked)
- claim: Graph-R1 beats StandardRAG, HyperGraphRAG and Search-R1 on average F1 over six QA sets, and the gap widens with model size.
  number: Avg F1 for Graph-R1 is 40.09 / 51.26 / 57.82 at 1.5B / 3B / 7B. Search-R1 at 7B is 46.19, StandardRAG (GPT-4o-mini) 32.05, HyperGraphRAG (GPT-4o-mini) 29.40.
  setup: Table 2. Backbones are Qwen2.5-1.5B/3B/7B-Instruct, trained with GRPO. Test sets are 2Wiki, HotpotQA, Musique, NQ, PopQA and TriviaQA, with 128 test questions each (so small samples). GPT-4o-mini was used for the graph baselines.
  quote: "Graph-R1 achieves steadily higher F1 scores: 40.09, 51.26, and 57.82."
  where: p.7, Sec 5.2; Table 2 on p.6.
- claim: Prompt-only GraphRAG methods are not better than plain chunk RAG. RL is what unlocks the graph.
  number: GPT-4o-mini avg F1 is GraphRAG 24.87, LightRAG 23.57, PathRAG 20.02, HippoRAG2 25.49, HyperGraphRAG 29.40, StandardRAG 32.05.
  setup: Table 2, GPT-4o-mini rows.
  quote: "Prompt-only GraphRAG methods often underperform StandardRAG, showing that graph structures alone are not sufficient."
  where: p.7 Sec 5.2; Table 2.
- claim: Ablation shows that removing any of knowledge construction, multi-turn interaction or RL hurts. RL matters most.
  number: Qwen2.5-3B, avg over 2Wiki and HotpotQA, F1: full 57.16; w/o K.C. 46.11; w/o M.I. 35.99; w/o R.L. 10.74. At 7B: 63.87 / 53.87 / 45.91 / 17.79.
  setup: Fig 5a ablation table, 2Wiki and HotpotQA only. "w/o R.L." means the untrained model.
  quote: "Graph-R1 50.00 57.56 55.78 76.45 50.78 56.75 54.74 77.46 50.39 57.16 55.26 76.96 w/o K.C.36.33 44.94 ... w/o R.L.0.78 8.91"

- claim: Retrieval representation ordering under RL is none < chunks < binary-relation graph < hypergraph.
  number: none
  setup: Figs 4 and 5b, step-wise F1 curves. The text gives no table for this.
  quote: "hypergraph-based knowledge with RL (red) achieves the highest ceiling."
  where: p.7 Sec 5.3.
- claim: GRPO beats PPO and REINFORCE++ here. A Qwen3-4B start, already RL-trained, has a slightly lower ceiling.
  number: none (curves only)
  setup: Fig 5e/5f, Graph-R1 3B.
  quote: "GRPO significantly outperforms REINFORCE++ (Hu et al., 2025) and PPO (Schulman et al., 2017), achieving the highest F1."
  where: p.7.
- claim: Construction cost is lower than the other GraphRAG methods, and answer-time cost is reported as $0.
  number: Graph-R1 7B: TP1KT 5.69 s, CP1MT $2.81, 120,499 nodes, 98,073 edges, TPQ 7.0 s, CP1KQ $0, F1 65.0. GraphRAG is 8.04 s / $3.35. HyperGraphRAG is 6.76 s / $4.14, with 9.6 s and $8.76 per 1K queries. HippoRAG2 is 3.25 s / $1.26, which is cheaper to build.
  setup: Table 6a, 2Wiki. The $0 reflects a local open model with no API at inference. Construction still uses GPT-4o-mini.
  quote: "Graph-R1 requires only 5.69 seconds and $2.81 per 1K tokens for knowledge construction, lower than GraphRAG (8.04s, $3.35) and HyperGraphRAG (6.76s, $4.14)."
  where: p.7-8 Sec 5.4; table on p.8.
- claim: Graph-R1 uses short responses and a few turns.
  number: about 1200-1500 tokens and 2.3-2.5 turns on average.
  setup: Fig 7a/7b, 3B, compared with Search-R1 and R1-Searcher. HotpotQA training curves.
  quote: "averaging around 1200-1500 tokens and 2.3-2.5 turns, leading to more stable and accurate retrieval."
  where: p.8 Sec 5.5.
- claim: Generation quality, judged by GPT-4o-mini on 7 criteria, is higher than Search-R1.
  number: Graph-R1 7B Overall 82.4 vs Search-R1 70.3. Correctness 86.9, Relevance 95.2, Logical Coherence 88.5.

  quote: "Graph-R1 achieves a much higher Overall score (82.4 vs. 70.3) than Search-R1"

  number: Format reward is 0.5 per valid step, capped at 1.0. R(tau) = -1 + Rformat + 1[Rformat=1]*F1. Top-k 5 facts per turn; GraphRAG baselines use top-60.

  where: p.4-5, p.18.

  number: 3B avg F1, I.I.D.: Search-R1 35.69 vs Graph-R1 51.26. Single O.O.D.: 25.28 vs 44.10. Combined: 35.25 vs 48.19. Zero-shot on five specialised domains (Medicine, Agriculture, CS, Legal, Mix), avg F1: 24.32 vs 39.26. HyperGraphRAG (GPT-4o-mini, taken from its own paper) is 38.61.
  setup: Appendix K, Tables 5-6, Qwen2.5-3B, model trained on the combined set for the specialised-domain test.
  quote: "Graph-R1 (3B) – 42.65 – 50.20 – 32.06 – 38.20 – 42.63 – 58.85 – 44.10"
  where: p.21.
- claim: Graph construction pipeline details.
  number: 1200-token chunks with a 50-token overlap. Each extracted n-ary fact gets a coherence score.
  setup: Appendix, Fig 12. GPT-4o-mini extractor, bge-large-en-v1.5 embeddings.
  quote: "each document is divided using a 1200-token window with a 50-token overlap"
  where: appendix near the end (p.20, unconfirmed).
- claim: Training and test data are sampled sizes.
  number: 5,120 train and 128 test per dataset.
  quote: "we uniformly sample 5,120 instances per dataset for training and 128 instances for testing."
  where: p.17 App D.

LIMITS
- There is no limitations section. The impact statement says only "This work poses no significant ethical concerns".
- Test sets are only 128 questions per dataset, so per-dataset differences are noisy. No seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests are reported.
- All data are Wikipedia-style QA (FlashRAG sets). There is no Cypher, no property-graph database and no text-to-query. The "graph" is an LLM-extracted n-ary hypergraph over text chunks, queried by embedding similarity. It is not a schema-bound KG.
- The graph is built with GPT-4o-mini, so construction still costs money. The "$0" is only inference.
- The GPT-4o-mini baselines (GraphRAG, LightRAG, etc.) are not RL-trained and use top-60 context, so the comparison mixes training with graph type. The one controlled comparison is Search-R1 (chunks plus RL). The text also mentions "R1+LightRAG (3B)" in Fig 5b, shown only as curves.
- Propositions 1-3 are "proved" by informal information-theoretic arguments (Lyapunov, Fano). These are heuristic, not rigorous. The paper says the proofs rest on assumptions such as "it is expected that rho_t >= rho_static".
- Qwen3-4B result: a model already RL-trained over-relies on its own reasoning.

BUILDS ON: DeepSeek-R1 (Guo et al., 2025a) and GRPO (Shao et al., 2024); Search-R1 (Jin et al., 2025a); R1-Searcher (Song et al., 2025); HyperGraphRAG (Luo et al., 2025a, the same group); GraphRAG (Edge et al., 2025); LightRAG (Guo et al., 2025b); PathRAG (Chen et al., 2026); HippoRAG2 (Gutierrez et al., 2025); RAG (Lewis et al., 2020); FlashRAG (Jin et al., 2025b) for datasets; bge-large-en-v1.5 embeddings (cited as Chen et al., 2023, BGE M3).

CODE: Prompt template (Table 1, p.4): "You are a helpful assistant. Answer the given question. You can query from knowledge base provided to you to answer the question. You can query knowledge as many times as you want. You must first conduct reasoning inside <think>...</think>. If you need to query knowledge, you can set a query statement between <query>...</query> ... When you have the final answer, you can output the answer inside <answer>...</answer>." Fusion score: Score(f) = 1/rV + 1/rH, with rank set to infinity if absent (eq 9; the extraction dropped the fraction bars).

FIGURES: Fig 1 (p.2) is the worked trajectory: think, query, retrieve hyperedges with coherence scores, rethink, answer. Fig 2 (p.2) is a bar chart of F1 across the six datasets. Fig 3 (p.3) is the framework overview. Fig 5 (p.7) holds the ablation table plus curves for representation, size and RL algorithm. Fig 6a (p.8) is the time and cost table. Fig 7 (p.8) shows response length, turns, and F1 against retrieved length. Fig 9 (p.13) is the full agent prompt with a worked trace. Fig 12 is the construction pipeline. Captions were taken from the extraction, not from the figures script.

PROBLEMS: No embedded instructions found.
- Text and table disagree: the Sec 5.2 text says "57.28 F1 under Qwen2.5-7B-Instruct", while Table 2 and the same paragraph's later line give 57.82. Use 57.82 (table).
- The text says "$2.81 per 1K tokens" while the table column is cost per 1M tokens (CP1MT). Use CP1MT.
- Table 6a is cited as "Table 6a" and "Figures 6" interchangeably. The Table 2 header glyphs (marking prompt vs training, chunk vs graph) were lost in extraction.
- The Fig 4 and 5 curve values are not extractable.
- Table 2's F1 column for 7B 2Wiki is 65.04, which matches the Fig 6a "F1 65.0" (the 7B 2Wiki-only value).
- Table 2's "Avg" columns are EM, F1, R-S, G-E.
- Relevance to target note 11-kg-rag-and-text-to-cypher.md: this paper is KG/hypergraph RAG with RL, with no text-to-Cypher content.
